deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp.16-18). Sigma = {Delta_i, i in I}, card I = n, is an arrangement of pseudo-lines in a topological projective plane X. X~ is the double cover (sphere). Gamma(Sigma) is a graph whose vertices are the isotopy classes of pseudo-lines D placed relative to Sigma (Pr(Sigma)). Its edges are elementary specialisations D -> D', where D is pushed through vertices of the arrangement. D is stable if it is in general position. It is critical if it passes through vertices of the arrangement. It is super-critical if D equals some Delta_{i0}. Str(Sigma) is a canonical cellular embedding of Gamma(Sigma) in a surface. Edges and the angular 'arcs' at each vertex carry weights in N*, and the weights around a vertex D sum to 2n (p.16).

This page.
(1) Combinatorial polygon. Pol(D) is the polygon read off along D. Its vertices are the points where D meets the arrangement (a vertex s of multiplicity k counts once with weight k). Its sides are the segments of D between them. Grothendieck 'blows up' each vertex into as many vertices as its weight. The result is a polygon P^(D) of even order 2n.
- P^(D) is realised by a contour D~ 'parallel to D'. The natural model is the boundary of a thin tubular (Moebius) neighbourhood of D in X, a circle that double-covers D.
- This contour meets every Delta_i twice and separates the Delta_i passing through a multiple point.
(2) Bijections. Let I~ be the set of oriented pseudo-lines (2n elements). There are canonical bijections between I~ and the edges/vertices of P^(D). Since P^(D) has even order it has an antipodism (the deck involution of D~ -> D). The bijections intertwine this antipodism with orientation reversal on I~.
(3) Example: D = Delta_{i0} super-critical. Then D has only generisation edges. These correspond to the points of the lift of Delta that lie over the vertices s on Delta. Each is weighted by the number of other Delta_i through s, i.e. the number of distinct crossings a parallel to Delta has near s. Blowing up gives (next page) a polygon of order 2(n-1), cut out on a parallel to Delta by the Delta_i (i != i0), with a bijection compatible with antipodism. That bijection depends on an orientation of Delta_{i0}; reversing it composes with the antipodism.
(4) Goal (next page). A canonical map from vertices of Gamma(Sigma) to antipodally compatible polygonal (cyclic) structures on I~, conjectured injective, followed by the study of how P, P^ vary along specialisations.

Modern reading. Gamma(Sigma)/Str(Sigma) is the (rank 3) extension space / poset of single-element extensions of the oriented matroid of Sigma, with weak maps as specialisations. P^(D) is the contraction of the extension at D: the rank-2 oriented matroid, i.e. the cyclic 'local sequence' of crossings along D, doubled antipodally. Injectivity in the stable case is immediate in chirotope terms. The extended chirotope is chi on I-triples plus chi(D,i,j), which is exactly the contraction data; topological representation (Folkman-Lawrence) then lifts this to isotopy.
errors: Cardinality slip (next page, prepared here). 'I minus {i0} ≃ set of vertices of P^(Delta_{i0})' cannot be a bijection, since the polygon has order 2(n-1) while I minus {i0} has n-1 elements. It must mean the oriented indices I~ minus {±i0}, or vertices modulo antipodism, or a choice of lift fixed by the orientation of Delta_{i0}.

Blowing up a multiple vertex into k vertices needs a linear order of the k lines through it. Taking a parallel on one side gives the reverse order from the other side. The construction is canonical only with the 'contour around D' (boundary of the Moebius neighbourhood) interpretation, which the text suggests but does not state.

Gap: for critical D, the blown-up polygon alone may not remember which crossings were simultaneous. Injectivity of vertices of Gamma(Sigma) -> polygonal structures relies on the two antipodal passages differing by local reversals. This is plausible but not argued; Grothendieck only says it 'should not be difficult'.

ideas.what: Graph/stratified surface of pseudo-line positions relative to an arrangement, with specialisation edges and weights
ideas.modern_name: Extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid (poset of single-element extensions, weak maps)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman-Pollack (cell complexes of configurations, early 1980s); Sturmfels-Ziegler, Extension spaces of oriented matroids (1993); MacPherson's combinatorial Grassmannian programme

ideas.what: Polygon of crossings along D, blown up by multiplicities on a parallel contour, of order 2n with antipodism matching orientation reversal
ideas.modern_name: Contraction / rank-2 local sequence (cyclic allowable sequence) at the new element, doubled to the antipodal cyclic order on I~
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman-Pollack (allowable and local sequences); Las Vergnas / Bland (contraction in oriented matroids)

ideas.what: Super-critical case D = Delta_{i0}: polygon of order 2(n-1) from crossings of the other lines, bijection depending on orientation, changed by antipodism
ideas.modern_name: Contraction of an oriented matroid at an element (local sequence of a pseudo-line)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard oriented matroid theory (Bland-Las Vergnas, Folkman-Lawrence)

ideas.what: Conjectured injective map from vertices of Gamma(Sigma) to antipodal polygonal structures on I~
ideas.modern_name: Extension determined by its contraction (chirotope chi(D,·,·)); localisation/cocircuit signature description of extensions

missed.claim: In 1983-84 Grothendieck independently sets up the extension space of a pseudo-line arrangement as a weighted cellular map on a surface (weights summing to 2n at each vertex). He encodes each extension by its antipodal contraction polygon. This parallels Goodman-Pollack and anticipates part of Sturmfels-Ziegler's (1993) study of rank-3 extension spaces. It is not recorded as Grothendieck's work.
missed.quote: en "éclatant" chaque sommet ... en autant de sommets que l'indique son poids ... Comme P^(D) est donc d'ordre pair il a des antipodismes, I~ aussi et la bijection est compatible avec les antipodismes.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit only. The mathematics is standard oriented-matroid theory. The weighted-map viewpoint (edge plus arc weights equal 2n at each vertex) is a mildly distinctive bookkeeping of the extension space as a surface map, in the spirit of his dessins/cartes.

deep.surprise_reason: Grothendieck is doing oriented-matroid / extension-space combinatorics essentially in parallel with Goodman-Pollack and before Sturmfels-Ziegler. That is historically interesting, but the content on this page (contraction polygons with antipodism, injectivity of the encoding) is routine in modern terms and largely known.
transcription_corrections: 'il n'y a pas que des arêtes de génératrices' should likely read 'il n'y a que des arêtes de générisation, issues de D'. The marginal NB also has 'générisation'. A super-critical D only has generisations.
In the marginal NB, 'génériques[?]' is probably 'générisation' (sommets of P^(D) coming from generisation edges).
'en ployant chaque arête' is uncertain; it may be 'en éclatant' or 'en subdivisant chaque arête ... autant de fois que l'indique son poids'.
'Δ^ (= relevé de Δ dans X~)' is probably '(= image inverse / revêtement de Δ dans X~)'. The sense is the lift to the double cover.
